- id: "1"
  title: Internal role gate rejects anonymous and role-less callers
  description: >-
    CAP-1. Make requireInternalProjectAccess decide identically to
    getInternalProjectAccessOrNull so anonymous and role-less identities are
    refused across every existing helper-guarded mutation, query, and action.
  done_checkpoint: true
  invoke_dev_with: >-
    Read SPEC.md CAP-1, touchpoints.md row CAP-1, and the Story 1 caller
    inventory first. Dependencies: none; this story must land before stories
    3, 6, and 9, which reuse the helper. Scope: all current direct and
    transitive requireInternalProjectAccess callers inherit the tightened rule:
    60 public mutations, four privileged public queries, and the two public
    project-copy/review actions recorded at gate G-11. Dashboard reads guarded
    only by requireCurrentUser and client share-token flows are unchanged.
    Acceptance: (1) direct helper parity for no/unmapped identity, stored
    anonymous with or without a role, mapped role-less, and writer/manager/admin;
    (2) updateReportContent and applyProposal rejection tests assert complete
    report/proposal rows and snapshot ids unchanged, with owner or elevated
    positive controls; (3) smoke-test the four queries and two actions listed
    in CAP-1 for typed stored-anonymous and role-less rejection; (4) preserve
    NOT_FOUND for an eligible actor and missing project. Gates G-1, G-2, G-4,
    and G-11 are source-verified in the approved Story 1 spec and inventory;
    recheck them if source changes before implementation. Do not rename public
    functions. Tests go in new convex/reportAuthz.test.ts.
- id: "2"
  title: Publish-for-review authorized by current Owner, Manager, or Admin
  description: >-
    CAP-3. Replace the creator-or-admin check in publishForReview with the
    role capability check per recorded decision D-2; the original creator is
    denied once they no longer hold an eligible role.
  spec_checkpoint: true
  invoke_dev_with: >-
    Read SPEC.md CAP-3 and decision D-2, plus touchpoints.md row CAP-3.
    Dependencies: none, but run after story 1 so the test setup is shared.
    Acceptance: after ownership transfer, new Owner can publish; Manager can
    publish; Admin can publish; original creator with none of those roles on
    the project is rejected; a signed-in internal user holding a project role
    G-1 identifies as ineligible (any internal role other than Owner,
    Manager, Admin; if G-1 finds none exists, record that and drop the case)
    is rejected; anonymous is rejected; no write on rejection (project status
    and report fields unchanged).
    Never read projects.createdBy for this decision. Verify (G-1): the
    capability constant in shared/capabilities.ts and requireCapability
    signature; docs/product-domain.md role matrix is authoritative if names
    differ. Extend convex/projects.test.ts (existence unverified).
- id: "3"
  title: Brain feedback scoped to accessible, matching report and project
  description: >-
    CAP-5. submitBrainFeedback rejects inaccessible reportId or projectId,
    a report whose projectId differs from the supplied projectId, and
    callers without an internal role.
  invoke_dev_with: >-
    Read SPEC.md CAP-5 and touchpoints.md row CAP-5. Dependency: story 1 must
    be complete; reuse its helper for the role and project check. Acceptance,
    each rejected before any write: (1) reportId caller cannot read;
    (2) projectId caller cannot access; (3) reportId whose projectId differs
    from supplied projectId; (4) caller with no internal role. Positive
    control: internal-role caller with matching accessible pair succeeds and
    the feedback row is written. Tests in convex/brainFeedback.test.ts
    (existence unverified; create if absent).
- id: "4"
  title: Client-edit acceptance snapshots before patch and is restorable
  description: >-
    CAP-4 part a. acceptEdit writes a report snapshot in the same mutation
    before patching text so restoring it returns the exact pre-accept prose.
  invoke_dev_with: >-
    Read SPEC.md CAP-4(a) and touchpoints.md row CAP-4a. Dependencies: none.
    Acceptance: (1) after acceptEdit a snapshot exists whose content equals
    the report text immediately before the accept; (2) restoring that
    snapshot through the existing restore path returns that text exactly;
    (3) if the patch fails the snapshot is not persisted (same transaction).
    Verify (G-10): existing snapshot kinds in convex/snapshots.ts; reuse one
    if it fits, else add one new kind value (allowed by the schema
    constraint) and record the choice. Reuse the snapshot writer applyProposal
    uses where possible. New test for acceptEdit (file name at planning's
    discretion).
- id: "5"
  title: Brain nomination only after writer review row is persisted
  description: >-
    CAP-4 part b. submitWriterReview enqueues Brain nomination only after
    the writerReviews insert succeeds, passing the persisted row id.
  invoke_dev_with: >-
    Read SPEC.md CAP-4(b) and touchpoints.md row CAP-4b. Dependencies: none.
    Acceptance: (1) on success the nomination is scheduled after the insert
    and receives the inserted review id; (2) when the insert fails
    (validation or thrown error) no nomination is scheduled and no
    writerReviews row exists; (3) existing callers unchanged. Verify (G-5,
    G-4): whether the nomination site is a mutation (scheduling is
    transactional with the insert, so ordering plus passing the persisted id
    satisfies the criterion) or an action (must await the mutation first);
    and how the test harness can assert scheduled functions, for example the
    _scheduled_functions system table under convex-test. New test for
    submitWriterReview.
- id: "6"
  title: markProposalApplied gains full apply parity with applyProposal
  description: >-
    CAP-2 per decision D-1. Keep the public one-by-one path and give it the
    same authorization recheck, pre_chat_edit snapshot, revision fence, atomic
    content plus status write, and revision bump as applyProposal.
  spec_checkpoint: true
  invoke_dev_with: >-
    Read SPEC.md CAP-2 and decision D-1, plus touchpoints.md row CAP-2.
    Dependency: story 1 complete (authorization helper). Do not delete
    markProposalApplied; do not leave the design choice open. Acceptance:
    (1) one-by-one apply yields proposal applied, a pre_chat_edit snapshot
    equal to the content just before the apply, and revisionNumber
    incremented by exactly one, all in one mutation; (2) second call with the
    same expectedRevisionNumber is rejected with a typed stale-revision error
    and leaves status, content, revision, and snapshot count unchanged;
    (3) authorization is rechecked inside the mutation; (4) no sequence of
    public calls yields applied without snapshot and bump. If the current
    function only flips status while the client writes content separately,
    move the content write for that proposal inside it. A shared internal
    helper with applyProposal is allowed, not required. Frontend: only
    src/lib/components/chat/ProposalCard.svelte changes; it passes
    expectedRevisionNumber (A-5) and shows the stale error without crashing;
    one-by-one UX otherwise identical. Add a component regression test for
    the one-by-one flow and run npm run test:component locally (CI does not
    run it). Backend tests in tests/chatProposals.test.ts (existence
    unverified). Verify (G-2): every caller of markProposalApplied.
- id: "7"
  title: Provider retry budget proven to fit the action limit
  description: >-
    CAP-6. Set the Anthropic client used by generateCandidate to maxRetries 1
    with a timeout that satisfies the budget inequality (4-minute target),
    and add a deterministic test over the imported configuration.
  invoke_dev_with: >-
    Read SPEC.md CAP-6, assumptions A-2 and A-4, and touchpoints.md row CAP-6.
    Dependencies: none. The normative requirement is the inequality, not the
    numbers. Acceptance: (1) the provider module exports named constants
    timeoutMs, maxRetries, sequentialCallsPerGenerateCandidate (calls),
    reservedNonRequestMs, actionLimitMs; (2) reservedNonRequestMs is a
    conservative named reserve covering maximum SDK retry backoff plus all
    remaining non-request action work, at least 60000 unless source evidence
    recorded at planning justifies another number; (3) a unit test imports
    the actual config (no literals copied into the test) and asserts
    calls * (maxRetries + 1) * timeoutMs + reservedNonRequestMs <
    actionLimitMs; (4) the test asserts maxRetries === 1; (5) the test
    asserts timeoutMs === 240000 only when calls === 1 and the verified
    actionLimitMs and reservedNonRequestMs make it satisfy the inequality;
    otherwise lower timeoutMs until the inequality holds and assert the
    lowered value instead. Not merely a config change. Verify (G-6, G-5):
    Anthropic SDK backoff semantics and ceiling (feeds the reserve); the
    number of sequential calls in generateCandidate; the Convex action limit
    (target 600000). Widen scope to other clients only if planning confirms
    they run in the same action budget. Test file at planning's discretion.
- id: "8"
  title: Superseded generations and typed QA refusal without a report
  description: >-
    CAP-7. retryFailedCandidates marks the original generation superseded
    (new status value) and requestReportQa returns a typed error for any
    generation without a report.
  spec_checkpoint: true
  invoke_dev_with: >-
    Read SPEC.md CAP-7, assumption A-1, and touchpoints.md row CAP-7.
    Dependencies: none. Acceptance: (1) after retryFailedCandidates the
    original has status superseded and the new generation continues;
    (2) history and stats readers exclude superseded (not completed, failed,
    or in progress); (3) retryFailedCandidates on a superseded generation is
    rejected; (4) requestReportQa on a generation with no report, including
    superseded, throws ConvexError with a stable code field and writes
    nothing. Schema: add superseded to generations.status union only;
    supersededBy is optional and only if a consumer needs it (record if
    added). Audit every consumer of generations.status (history, stats,
    dashboards, reaper) for the new value. Extend
    convex/generationRecovery.test.ts (existence unverified).
- id: "9"
  title: Bounded chat context, windowed proposals, empty reads on missing threads
  description: >-
    CAP-8. Cap model context at 30 non-tool messages, bound listProposals to
    the loaded turn window, and return [] for nonexistent or deleted threads
    while still erroring on unauthorized reads.
  invoke_dev_with: >-
    Read SPEC.md CAP-8 and decision D-5, plus touchpoints.md row CAP-8.
    Dependency: story 1 complete (authorization semantics for the
    unauthorized case). Acceptance: (1) the streamText call uses a context
    options constant with recentMessages 30 and tool messages excluded; test
    asserts the constant and, if the agent library exposes it, that a thread
    of 35 messages with 5 tool messages yields at most 30 non-tool messages;
    (2) listProposals accepts the same optional window arguments as
    listTurns with identical defaults and returns only proposals whose turn
    is in that window; a proposal on a turn outside the window is absent;
    (3) listMessages and listProposals return [] for a nonexistent or
    deleted thread; (4) an existing thread the caller cannot access still
    throws the existing authorization error, not []; (5) existing callers
    keep an unchanged call shape (no new required args, source compatible);
    their results are intentionally bounded by the default listTurns window
    and may omit proposals on turns outside it, which is the intended change,
    not a regression. Verify (G-5, G-2): agent library contextOptions field
    names; listTurns window args. Extend
    convex/chatTurns.test.ts (existence unverified).
- id: "10"
  title: Generations record prompt version hash and learning digest ids
  description: >-
    CAP-9 part a. New generations store promptVersion (hash of the stable
    prompt program) and learningDigestIds (union of digests sent in provider
    payloads); aiUsage rows carry generationId, candidateRunId, durationMs
    with a by_generationId index.
  spec_checkpoint: true
  invoke_dev_with: >-
    Read SPEC.md CAP-9, decision D-4, assumption A-3, and touchpoints.md row
    CAP-9a. Dependencies: none; story 11 depends on this. Acceptance: (1) a
    generation created after the change has promptVersion equal to a
    deterministic hash of the stable prompt program (static system
    templates, instructions, relevant prompt configuration; excludes runtime
    project, report, transcript, and digest content), written at creation or
    before the first provider call; two generations on the same prompt
    program with different project content share the hash, and a changed
    template changes it; record the hashed input list and algorithm;
    (2) learningDigestIds is the deduplicated union of digest ids whose
    content is included in any provider request payload for the generation,
    recorded or updated immediately before each payload is handed to the
    provider SDK (expected anchors: assembly sites in pipeline.ts and
    iterative.ts), growing across a multi-call generation and final at
    terminal status; a digest fetched but not sent is absent; empty array
    when none; (3) every provider call made on behalf of a generation that
    returns usage writes an aiUsage row with generationId, candidateRunId
    when applicable, and durationMs, including calls whose generation later
    fails or is retried; calls that return no usage write no row and no
    synthetic zero-token rows are written; (4) legacy rows are untouched and
    readers tolerate absent fields. Schema: optional fields only plus index
    by_generationId following existing naming. No backfill. Verify (G-7):
    aiUsage cost field and unit. Tests in tests/aiUsage.test.ts (existence
    unverified).
- id: "11"
  title: getGeneration exposes attributable cost with legacy null semantics
  description: >-
    CAP-9 part b. getGeneration returns cost as the sum of recorded aiUsage
    rows keyed by generationId for tracked generations and null for legacy
    ones.
  invoke_dev_with: >-
    Read SPEC.md CAP-9 and decision D-4, plus touchpoints.md row CAP-9b.
    Dependency: story 10 complete. cost is strictly the sum of recorded
    aiUsage cost rows for the generation; it documents recorded attributable
    cost, not exact total provider spend or invoice completeness, and the
    field documentation says so. Acceptance: (1) tracked generation
    (promptVersion present) with usage rows returns cost equal to the sum
    of those rows in the unit stored on aiUsage, including failed and
    retried call rows; (2) tracked generation with no rows returns cost 0;
    (3) legacy generation returns promptVersion, learningDigestIds, and
    cost all null, never 0; (4) an in-flight tracked generation returns the
    sum so far and learningDigestIds as recorded so far; (5) any caller
    authorized to read the generation sees the fields, and an Admin can read
    them for any generation. Aggregate via the by_generationId index inside
    the query; confirm the per-generation row count is bounded by the
    pipeline (G-7). Do not add UI. Tests alongside story 10.
- id: "12"
  title: Confirmed unlearn with failure evidence and retry-free embeds
  description: >-
    CAP-10. unlearnSource writes unlearn_confirmed only after confirmed or
    already-absent erasure, keeps evidence on failure, is idempotent, and
    embedSource never restores or retries a revoked source.
  spec_checkpoint: true
  invoke_dev_with: >-
    Read SPEC.md CAP-10 and touchpoints.md row CAP-10. Dependencies: none.
    Acceptance, one test each: (a) live ragEntryId and confirmed erasure:
    exactly one unlearn_confirmed audit row, ragEntryId cleared, source not
    approved; (b) remote reports already absent, or source never had
    ragEntryId: same outcome as (a); (c) erasure fails: no unlearn_confirmed
    row, ragEntryId retained, source not approved and not servable, error
    surfaced to caller, failure evidence recorded (existing audit action if
    one fits, else the optional unlearn_failed value; record the choice);
    (d) second revoke after (a): no error, no remote call, no second
    unlearn_confirmed row; (e) embedSource on missing, revoked, or otherwise
    non-approved source returns normally, writes no ragEntryId, schedules no
    retry; (f) embed completing remotely after revoke: source not approved,
    entry not served, no embedding retry; the completion path runs
    compensating erasure of the newly created remote entry; if compensation
    confirms deletion or already-absent, ragEntryId is not written and
    status is unchanged; if compensation fails, retain the remote id as
    evidence (ragEntryId, or the planning-gated additive evidence field if
    G-8 finds ragEntryId unsuitable), keep the source non-approved and
    non-servable, record failure evidence via the same mechanism as (c), and
    schedule or surface deletion-only remediation; never write
    unlearn_confirmed for that late entry until compensation is confirmed.
    Test (f) in both branches: compensation succeeds and compensation fails.
    Mirror the late-completion fence in convex/ai/brain/rag.ts for the
    status check. Do not invent remote API details; verify (G-8) how the RAG
    client signals confirmed and already absent, which deletion call the
    compensation path reuses, and whether ragEntryId can hold the orphaned
    id without being read as servable. Schema: brainAuditLog action adds
    unlearn_confirmed; unlearn_failed optional; evidence field optional and
    planning-gated. Tests in convex/brainFeedback.test.ts or a new brain
    test file.
- id: "13"
  title: Reaper walks every eligible project by index in bounded pages
  description: >-
    CAP-11. Add a projects index on status and replace the take(500) scan
    with paged, cursor-continued iteration over eligible statuses so every
    project is reached without an unbounded transaction.
  invoke_dev_with: >-
    Read SPEC.md CAP-11 and decision D-6, plus touchpoints.md row CAP-11.
    Dependency (hard): story 8 must be complete so the reaper's status
    handling already accounts for superseded; do not start before it lands. Acceptance: (1) projects has an index
    on status named per the existing by_* convention; (2) the reaper reads
    eligible statuses through that index with cursor or last-key
    continuation at a fixed, test-overridable page size, one page per
    transaction, until exhausted; (3) deterministic test seeds more than 500
    eligible projects each with a stale generation, or seeds a small set
    with page size overridden below the seed count, and asserts every stale
    generation is reaped, non-eligible projects are untouched, and no single
    transaction reads more than one page; (4) take(500) is gone. Verify
    (G-5, G-9): which pagination primitive is valid inside the reaper's
    function type per convex/_generated/ai/guidelines.md; the eligible
    status set; existing projects indexes. New reaper test at planning's
    discretion.

  description: >-

  spec_checkpoint: true
  invoke_dev_with: >-

- id: "10"
  title: Generations record prompt version hash and learning digest ids

    deleted thread; (4) an existing thread the caller cannot access still

    keep an unchanged call shape (no new required args, source compatible);

    program with different project content share the hash, and a changed
    template changes it; record the hashed input list and algorithm;

    content is included in any provider request payload for the generation,
    recorded or updated immediately before each payload is handed to the
    provider SDK (expected anchors: assembly sites in pipeline.ts and
    iterative.ts), growing across a multi-call generation, including generation-owned

    returns usage writes an aiUsage row with generationId, candidateRunId
    when applicable, and durationMs, including calls whose generation later
    fails or is retried; calls that return no usage write no row and no
    synthetic zero-token rows are written; (4) legacy rows are untouched and

    (promptVersion present) with usage rows returns cost equal to the sum
    of those rows in the unit stored on aiUsage, including failed and
    retried call rows; (2) tracked generation with no rows returns cost 0;
    (3) legacy generation returns promptVersion, learningDigestIds, and
    cost all null, never 0; (4) an in-flight tracked generation returns the
    sum so far and learningDigestIds as recorded so far; (5) any caller
    authorized to read the generation sees the fields, and an Admin can read
